title: The life of a program: from source file to process

videos.script: Lesson 1 compiled a file and ran it. This lesson follows the same program further, from the file on disk to a process the operating system can list. {{compile}} First the two commands again, done properly. The class files go in a directory of their own, and java is told where to look with the class path. The program takes arguments, and it ends with a number that the shell can read. {{wrong}} Then the three ways people ask java for the wrong thing, and the message each one prints. They all say the same words, so you learn to read the name inside them. {{launcher}} After that, a shortcut. java can run a source file directly, compiling it in memory, and since Java 22 it can do that for a program spread over several files. {{process}} Last, the program while it runs. Every JVM is a process with a number, threads you did not start, and memory you can measure. jps finds it, and jcmd asks it questions. By the end you can say where each part of a running Java program came from.
